jobs.title: Executive Director - Mental Health Client Action Network(MHCAN)
jobs.description:
**The Organization**

The Mental Health Client Action Network (MHCAN) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to supporting adults in Santa Cruz County with lived experience of mental health challenges. Founded nearly 40 years ago as an independent peer support center, MHCAN is actively transitioning its operational framework to an accredited Clubhouse Model of Services.

In alignment with Clubhouse standards, MHCAN operates as a member-driven community where participants ("members") and staff work side-by-side to run daily center operations, build social connections, and pursue employment, education, and wellness goals. All MHCAN staff members share lived experience with a mental health condition and/or navigating the mental health system.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of MHCAN and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, program management, community engagement, and resource development. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director ensures the organization stays true to its core mission of peer empowerment while successfully guiding the agency through its transition to the Clubhouse model and maintaining strong alignment with County Behavioral Health.

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE / 40 hours per week) exempt position.

**Compensation:** $95,000 – $105,000 annually, depending on experience.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Human Resources & Staff Leadership (25%)**

* Hire, train, supervise, and mentor all program staff and peer support team members.
* Foster a positive, supportive, and accountable organizational culture centered on lived experience and recovery.
* Manage staff scheduling, performance evaluations, and team development.
* Partner with the Fiscal Agent (FSAS) on HR policy enforcement, workplace safety, and personnel administration.

**Program Oversight & Clubhouse Model Transition (25%)**

* Lead the agency’s transition to and ongoing operation of a certified Clubhouse model of services.
* Ensure daily program activities effectively meet client needs and contract objectives.
* Evaluate program outcomes and implement continuous service delivery improvements.
* Monitor compliance with grant deliverables and County service agreements.

**Organizational Leadership & Strategy (20%)**

* Implement the organization's mission, vision, and strategic goals, serving as a passionate advocate for peer support.
* Develop annual organizational objectives in close collaboration with the Board of Directors and the County contract monitor.
* Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable legal and nonprofit regulatory standards.
* Provide monthly performance, operational, and financial reports to the Board.

**Community Relations & County Partnership (15%)**

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for MHCAN.
* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

**Financial Oversight & Fiscal Agent Coordination (5%)**

* Develop and manage the annual operating budget (approximately $590,000) in partnership with the Board and Fiscal Agent.
* Collaborate directly with Front St. Administrative Services to oversee fiduciary practices, review monthly financial statements, and ensure budget alignment. *(Note: Daily bookkeeping, payroll processing, and accounting entries are performed directly by the Fiscal Agent.)*

  

**Qualifications**

* **Lived Experience:** Lived experience as a person with a mental health condition and/or direct experience navigating the mental health system is required.
* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.
* **Leadership Experience:** Minimum 2–3 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a nonprofit or community service environment.
* **Management & Budgeting:** Demonstrated experience supervising staff, managing program operations, and overseeing grant/contract deliverables.
* **Skills:** Strong communication, interpersonal, and project management skills with the ability to build consensus across diverse community stakeholders.

**Performance Expectations**

* Maintain a balanced annual budget in coordination with the Fiscal Agent.
* Ensure successful transition and operational implementation of the Clubhouse model.
* Provide consistent leadership, accountability, and support to program staff.
* Maintain strong, transparent relationships with the Board of Directors, County Behavioral Health, and community partners.
* Ensure timely completion of grant reports and contract deliverables.

**Working Conditions & Physical Requirements**

* Standard office environment with high levels of interpersonal interaction.
* Computer and telephone usage for extended periods.
* Occasional evening or weekend attendance at Board meetings or community events.
* Local travel within Santa Cruz County.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

**Reporting Relationship:** Reports directly to the MHCAN Board of Directors.

jobs.title: Executive Director Epic Revenue Cycle Applications
jobs.description:
Description:

**Summary:**

Our client is a multi-hospital, nonprofit health system on the West Coast with a strong reputation for clinical quality. The organization is committed to a culture of respect, innovation, and collaboration, and supports leaders at every level in growing professionally.

This senior EHR Services leader will own the strategy, delivery, and ongoing performance of the organization’s Epic revenue cycle application portfolio, including evaluation, implementation, optimization, and support. You will lead a team of application professionals and act as a trusted partner to operational and executive leadership, translating business goals into technology roadmaps, budgets, and investment proposals.

You will also help shape the broader application strategy, working alongside fellow IS leaders to deliver a unified, service-oriented department. Additional incentive compensation may be available.

**\*\*This role is on-site 3-4 days per week at our client site in Los Angeles so someone local to the area is preferred.\*\***

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Serve as a core member of the senior IS leadership team, contributing to governance of the enterprise application portfolio.
* Partner with clinical, physician, and operational leaders, along with best-practice and governance groups, to develop and sustain application solutions that meet organizational needs.
* Ensure current and proposed system architectures support enterprise goals.
* Guide the design, build, and implementation of integrated, end-to-end software solutions.
* Track healthcare IT trends and emerging technologies to anticipate future needs.
* Advise the CIO, IT vice presidents, and executive leaders on technology direction, with regular written and in-person updates on projects and systems.
* Define, communicate, and enforce standards for systems, infrastructure, and software.
* Hire, coach, evaluate, and develop staff, including individual career-path planning.
* Establish application management policies and procedures that protect system integrity and availability.
* Oversee service level agreements with end-user departments through monitoring and performance management.
* Contribute to enterprise disaster recovery and business continuity planning.
* Respond quickly and constructively to emerging priorities and ad hoc needs.
* Comply with all IS policies and standards, including project management methodology, security requirements, and HIPAA privacy and security rules governing ePHI.

Requirements:

**Required:**

* 15+ years of experience in a healthcare delivery environment.
* 10+ years in management and leadership roles.
* Deep working knowledge of Epic, its revenue cycle modules, and supporting infrastructure.
* Hands-on experience with requirements gathering and business analysis.
* Proven background in systems, software, and integration design and development.
* Strong grasp of information processing principles, current systems software, protocols, and standards.
* Experience evaluating software and leading projects from planning through delivery.
* Exceptional analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving ability.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex ideas in plain language.
* Excellent architecture and technical documentation skills.
* Consultative, interpersonal, and collaborative leadership style.
* Ability to prioritize and perform in a high-pressure environment.
* Ability to research emerging technologies, standards, and products.
* Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or a related field.

**Preferred:**

* Master’s degree
* Current Epic certification(s)

jobs.title: Managing Director, Strategy and Partnerships
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

The Managing Director, Strategic Partnerships will lead City Year Bay Area’s strategy for building, stewarding, and growing high-impact external partnerships that advance the site’s mission, deepen community investment, and expand opportunities for students, AmeriCorps members, staff, alumni, and partners across the Bay Area.

**Job Description**

**Minimum Qualifications**

* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in strategic partnerships, fundraising, business development, external engagement, corporate relations, community affairs, or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience managing senior-level external relationships and translating organizational priorities into partnership strategies, proposals, communications, and stewardship plans.
* Experience working cross-functionally with senior leaders and internal teams to manage complex projects, relationships, events, or initiatives.
* Authorized documentation to work in the United States of America.
* Criminal background history clearance to work with school-age children, depending on position requirements.

**Responsibilities**

The Managing Director of strategic Partnerships will perform the following roles and responsibilities as described below:

**Strategic Partnership Development, External Engagement** **& Executive Communications**

* Develop and lead a comprehensive strategic partnerships plan that strengthens relationships with corporations, foundations, civic leaders, community organizations, alumni, school partners, and other external stakeholders while identifying and managing high-value opportunities that advance City Year Bay Area’s strategic priorities, revenue and engagement goals, and visibility for impact.
* Build and manage a comprehensive project plan for a $16M, four-year investment to expand City Year Bay Area’s work in Eastside San José, coordinating internal teams, external partners, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and decision points to ensure strong execution and alignment with sitewide priorities.
* Represent City Year Bay Area in external meetings, partner convenings, community events, and other forums with credibility, professionalism, and a strong understanding of the organization’s mission, model, and impact.
* Prepare executive briefings, talking points, partner profiles, meeting materials, stewardship updates, and other communications that equip the Executive Director and senior leaders to advance strategic relationships.
* Translate City Year Bay Area’s impact, program model, and strategic priorities into compelling narratives for funders, corporate partners, public officials, school partners, and community stakeholders.
* Monitor local partnership trends, community needs, education and workforce development priorities, and philanthropic opportunities to inform proactive partnership strategy.

**Revenue, Stewardship & Partnership Portfolio Management**

* Partner with the Executive Director, Development team, and site leadership to support corporate, philanthropic, and community investment strategies that help City Year Bay Area reach its $2.7M private revenue goal, including cultivation, proposal development, sponsorship opportunities, stewardship touchpoints, and renewal planning.
* Manage a portfolio of strategic partnership relationships, ensuring each relationship has clear goals, defined next steps, strong documentation, and consistent follow-through.
* Develop metrics, dashboards, briefings, and reporting tools to evaluate partnership health, return on engagement, stakeholder satisfaction, and alignment with City Year Bay Area priorities.

**Cross-Functional Partnership Strategy & Internal Alignment**

* Work closely with the Chief of Staff to ensure partnership strategy is aligned with sitewide priorities, executive communications, board engagement, staff capacity, and cross-departmental planning.
* Collaborate with Development, Impact, People & Operations, Recruitment, Marketing & Communications, and national teams to design well-coordinated, mission-aligned, and operationally feasible partner experiences, supported by clear internal systems and communication routines that keep teams aligned on commitments, opportunities, deliverables, deadlines, and decision points.

**Leadership, Collaboration & Learning**

* Lead project teams, consultants, or staff as assigned, setting clear expectations, managing performance, and fostering an environment of belonging, collaboration, accountability, and inclusion.
* Role model a growth mindset and commitment to City Year’s culture and values as a senior leader within a youth-serving organization.
* Perform additional responsibilities as assigned by the Executive Director to advance City Year Bay Area’s mission and strategic priorities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business, public policy, education, communications, external affairs, or a related field, or comparable professional experience.
* Experience in a nonprofit, education, youth development, workforce development, national service, corporate social responsibility, foundation, or public-private partnership setting.
* Demonstrated success developing or managing strategic partnerships that support revenue generation, volunteer engagement, thought leadership, events, community engagement, or multi-year initiatives, including experience contributing to strategies that help secure major annual funding priorities such as an approximately $1.5M challenge match and an approximately $3M sitewide private revenue target.
* Experience working with executive leaders, board members, corporate partners, public officials, school districts, philanthropic partners, or community coalitions.
* Comfort using CRM,(Salesforce) project management, presentation, and collaboration tools to track relationships, analyze engagement, and manage follow-through.
* City Year, AmeriCorps, or national service experience is a plus.

The Managing Director, Marketing and Communications will lead City Year Bay Area’s marketing, communications, brand, and external engagement strategy in support of the organization’s mission, visibility, fundraising, school partnership, recruitment, and stakeholder engagement goals.

**Job Description**

**Minimum Qualifications**

* At least eight years of progressively responsible experience in marketing, communications, public relations, media relations, external affairs, or nonprofit communications.
* At least three years of experience managing staff, consultants, vendors, or cross-functional teams.
* Demonstrated experience developing and implementing organization-wide marketing, communications, or stakeholder engagement strategies.

* Anticipate communications challenges and opportunities across the organization and develop proactive strategies that support clarity, alignment, visibility, and confidence among internal and external stakeholders.

**Executive Communications and Stakeholder Engagement**

* Develop executive-level communications including talking points, remarks, presentations, briefings, op-eds, letters, newsletters, stakeholder updates, and partner-facing materials.
* Partner with Development and site leadership to create high-quality communications that support donor cultivation, stewardship, corporate partnerships, grants, events, and external meetings.
* Collaborate with Impact and school partnership teams to communicate student impact, AmeriCorps member service, partnership outcomes, and the value of student success coaching.

* Partner with departments across the site to ensure internal and external communications are coordinated, accurate, timely, and aligned to organizational priorities.
* Support internal communications planning for major initiatives, organizational updates, staff engagement, leadership messages, and change management efforts.
* Build strong relationships with staff across departments to identify communications needs, elevate stories, and ensure consistent messaging across the organization.
* Develop tools, templates, calendars, and systems that improve communications planning, collaboration, and execution across teams.

* Lead communications strategy for major organizational events, stakeholder engagements, fundraising moments, service days, AmeriCorps member celebrations, and community-facing activities.
* Oversee the development of event messaging, scripts, speaker briefings, invitations, run-of-show language, presentation materials, and post-event communications.
* Partner with event owners and cross-functional teams to ensure major public moments reinforce City Year Bay Area’s brand, mission, values, and strategic priorities.

jobs.title: Pride Center Program Director (Student Services Professional IV)
jobs.description:
**Job no:** 562321
  
**Work type:** Staff
  
**Location:** San Diego
  
**Categories:** Unit 4 - APC - Academic Professionals of California, Probationary, Full Time, Student Services, On-site (work in-person at business location)
  
Position Description

**Position Summary**

San Diego State University is seeking an engaged and collaborative **Program Director** to lead the Pride Center and advance its mission of supporting LGBTQIA+ students’ belonging, well-being, leadership development, and academic success. Reporting to the Associate Chief Diversity Officer for Student Affairs and Campus Diversity, this role provides leadership for the Center’s programs, services, staff, budget, facilities, and daily operations.

The Program Director serves as a trusted resource and advocate for LGBTQIA+ students while working closely with faculty, staff, campus departments, community partners, and external organizations. This highly visible position offers the opportunity to shape inclusive initiatives, strengthen student support networks, and contribute to a more connected and equitable campus community.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the day-to-day operations of the Pride Center, including staff guidance, student employee support, and program administration and facilitation.
* Support the Center’s strategic direction by developing programs, services, initiatives, and assessment practices that respond to student needs.
* Oversee the Center’s budget, purchasing, resource stewardship, reports, and compliance with University policies and procedures.
* Provide advocacy, mentorship, and support to LGBTQIA+ students while responding thoughtfully to complex student, equity, mental health, and community concerns.
* Build collaborative relationships across campus and with community partners to strengthen student success, retention, academic achievement, leadership development, and belonging.
* Represent the Pride Center and Division of Student Affairs and Campus Diversity through outreach, communications, campus committees, events, and community engagement.

**Why Join Us?**

* Make a meaningful difference in the experiences, success, and well-being of LGBTQIA+ students at SDSU.
* Lead a highly visible campus center that connects student support, advocacy, education, and community-building.
* Collaborate with dedicated colleagues, faculty, staff, students, alumni, and community partners across a dynamic university environment.
* Help shape future programs, partnerships, and campus initiatives that advance equity, inclusion, and student belonging.

  

**Position Information**

* This is a full-time (1.0 time-base), benefits eligible, permanent/probationary position.
* This position is designated as exempt under FLSA and is not eligible for overtime compensation.
* Standard SDSU work hours are Monday – Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but may vary based on operational needs.
* The individual hired into this role will work on campus at SDSU in San Diego

  

**Department Summary**

The Pride Center at San Diego State University fosters an open, inclusive, safe, and affirming environment for individuals of all sexual orientations, romantic orientations, gender identities, and gender expressions, as well as their allies. Through community-building initiatives, advocacy, educational opportunities, and social justice programming, the Center supports students, staff, faculty, community members, and allies connected to the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.

Recognizing that identity is dynamic and continually evolving, the Pride Center is committed to creating a space where all 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals feel seen, accepted, and valued. Students of all backgrounds who are interested in engaging with the Center are welcome to participate in its programs and services.

For more information regarding the SDSU Pride Center, click here.

  

**Education and Experience**

Equivalent to graduation from a four-year college or university in a related field plus upper division or graduate course work in counseling techniques, interviewing and conflict resolution where such are job related.

Possession of the below required knowledge and abilities is typically demonstrated through the equivalent to four years of progressively responsible professional student services work experience which includes experience in advising students individually and in groups, and in analysis and resolution of complex student services problems.

A master’s degree in counseling, Clinical Psychology, Social Work, or a job-related field may be substituted for one year of professional experience. A doctorate degree and the appropriate internship or clinical training in counseling, guidance or a job-related field may be substituted for two years of the required professional experience for positions with a major responsibility for professional, personal or career counseling.

  

**Key Qualifications**

* Experience developing and coordinating programs that promote student belonging, well-being, leadership development, and academic success.
* Background working in student affairs, student services, advising, or a student support program.
* Knowledge of issues affecting LGBTQIA+ students and communities, with a commitment to creating an inclusive and affirming campus environment.
* Experience managing day-to-day operations, programs, staffing needs, budgets, and other resources.
* Skill in supporting students through complex situations while balancing advocacy, empowerment, institutional responsibilities, and appropriate professional boundaries.
* Ability to build collaborative relationships with campus departments, faculty, staff, community organizations, and cultural centers.
* Sound judgment, discretion, and conflict-management skills when responding to sensitive or challenging concerns.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Specialized training in conflict resolution, mediation, leadership, or organizational development.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Operations & Grants Mgmt
jobs.description:
**Deputy Director, Operations and Grants Management**

**TH****E COMPANY:**

Low Income Investment Fund (LIIF) is a national community development financial institution (CDFI), headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York City, Atlanta, Los Angeles and Washington, D.C., that invests in communities of opportunity, equity and well-being. As a CDFI, LIIF supports projects that have high social value but lack access to traditional financial institutions. Since 1984, LIIF has deployed more than $3.1 billion to serve more than two million people in communities across the country from its five offices. An S&P-rated organization, LIIF funds healthy communities by providing innovative capital solutions. Currently, LIIF is driving $5 billion in investments to advance racial equity (2020-2030). More on LIIF can be found at liifund.org.

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Deputy Director, Grants Management and Operations (Director) reports to the Vice President of Operations, who oversees all Operations team at LIIF. The Operations department was created in 2023 and consist of Information Technology (IT), Data Management (DM), and Portfolio Loan Servicing (PA) teams. The Deputy Director will be responsible for managing the grants management function within the operations team and supporting the VP Operations to oversee all operational functions. This position will be responsible for overseeing the administrative and budget measurement for all grants and contracts for the Programs team of the Low Income Investment Fund (LIIF). In addition, the Deputy Director will review all contracts to ensure compliance related task and key revenue recognition items are identified.

**REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS:**

The Deputy Director is responsible for efficient and compliant management of the philanthropic grants and public sector contracts that fund the work of LIIF’s Programs team. This position requires financial analysis, problem solving, and relationship building skills. It requires the ability to lead projects, collaborate across teams, and analyze financial data. The Deputy Director will serve as liaison between the Programs team, Finance team and other departments as needed to ensure efficient and economically sustainable operations relating to ensuring compliance, accurate grant accounting and budget management.

The Deputy Director will management 1-2 team members who will be responsible to all programmatic billing, creating all reclassification entries for the general ledger, provide the finance team with all general ledger support and manage the budget to actual monthly review process.

The ideal candidate will have broad knowledge of public and private grant and contract management; a team and service-oriented approach to working with colleagues, funders, and partners; a commitment to proactively problem solving; and an interest in being part of an organization committed to creating communities of opportunity, equity and well-being. Direct experience with state and local agency, foundations, and Federal funding is required.

**ES****S****E****NTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**Grants and Contracts Management:**

* Partners directly with Finance department and Programmatic departments (ex: Early childhood Education, National Program, and Fundraising) to review contract and grant applications and budgets prior to submission to funders.
* Lead negotiations in conjunction with the ECE and Program team prior to contract execution to ensure mission and profitability targets.
* For complex grant agreements, prepare revenue recognition memo for review by Finance team and sign off.
* Review all revenue recognition memo prepared by Finance team.
* Manage and oversees 1-2 team members whose primary responsibility will be reparation of financial reports and invoices for billing submissions.
* From operations side, review Salesforce to ensure all grant awards are properly included and identified.
* Review and at times, prepare financial reports from MIP, Concur and Adaptive systems to monitor grant and contract budgets, expenditures.
* Review and at times, prepare monthly/ quarterly / annual budget to actual analysis for all grants and contracts.
* Lead monthly meetings with program team, to review budget to actual results and identify any areas of concern related to budget management, such as, and not limited to, over/under spending, allocation issues and unallowable costs.
* Responsible for reviewing all proposed budget reallocations and budget contract modifications prior to submission (identification to be performed by grants manager)
* Responsible for reviewing all journal entries related to billings corrections.
* Present all journal entries and billing submissions to the Program Department for approval
* Submit all invoices to grantors for payment.
* Ensure information is transferred to the Finance Department to ensure monthly financial data is properly captured within the general ledger system.
* Review AR aging schedule (prepared by the Finance department) on monthly basis
* Review Net Asset releases (prepared by the Finance department) on a monthly basis.
* Leads effective communication strategy with Finance and program budget leads.
* Ensure grants/contracts are released as planned, invoices are complete and timely, and payments are applied appropriately.
* Review staff allocations to grants and contracts prepared by Program team ensuring allocation is allowable and fully documented for billing purposes.
* Assist Finance team in identifying new grants management systems and general ledger systems.

**Operations and Compliance:**

* Manage grant compliance and reporting, including adherence to grant budgets and tracking financial progress toward organizational and programmatic outcomes and goals.
* Collaborate with Finance, Development, Legal, and other departments to ensure grants and contracts are appropriately vetted, approved, and budgeted.
* Work closely with all departments throughout the life of the grants/co

jobs.title: DISTRICT EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, FOUNDATION
jobs.description:
**DISTRICT EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, FOUNDATION**  
  
**San Jose/Evergreen Community College District**

**Close/First Review Date:** 10/25/2026  
**Work Location:** District Office  
  
**Position Description:**  

**POSITION****SUMMARY**
  
  
The District Executive Director of Foundation reports to the Chancellor at the District Office. This is a full time, 12 months per year, classified management position.  
  
**POSITION****PURPOSE**

8. Develops, implements, establishes, and maintains policies, processes, and procedures for the Foundation; monitors and evaluates service quality; recommends, develops, and implements

**Mentor Community Services**, a part of the Sevita family, provides community-based services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Here we believe every person has the right to live well, and everyone deserves to have a fulfilling career. You’ll join a mission-driven team and create relationships that motivate us all every day. Join us today, and experience a career well lived.

  

**Program Director, IDD Services**

*$70,304/yr*

*M-F, 8am-5pm*

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.

* Manage the day-to-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.

* **Bachelor's degree required and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.**
* **1 year Program Director experience required**
* **1 year experience working with DD population required.**

* Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
* Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi-task to meet deadlines.
* Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
* A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.

***Why Join Us?***

* Full, Part-time, and As Needed schedules available.
* Full compensation/benefits package for full-time employees.

* Paid time off and holiday pay.
* Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.

jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Senior Director of Operations provides organization wide leadership for Bethany House, helping ensure that its shelters, programs, and administrative functions have the people, systems, resources and support needed to operate safely, effectively and consistently.

This is a hands-on leadership role that requires both strategic perspective and practical problem-solving. The Senior Director of Operations will oversee and coordinate key operational functions, strengthen systems and accountability, support organizational and staff development, identify and address operational risks. The Senior Director of Operations will work closely with the leadership team, Board of Directors, external partners and stakeholders to enhance operations across the organization.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Executive Partnership and Organizational Leadership**

Partner with the Executive Director to set priorities and move key initiatives from decision to completion.

* Represent the Executive Director and Bethany House in appropriate internal and external matters.
* Identify operational risks with solution-oriented intervention.

**Operations, Systems, and Accountability**

· Coordinate operational functions across programs, shelters, administration, human resources, facilities, and other support areas.

· Create clear systems for accountability, communication, deadlines, and follow-through.

· Review and improve policies, procedures, workflows, purchasing practices, contracts, and administrative systems.

· Coordinate work that crosses departments and mediate issues that require shared ownership.

**Leadership and Staff Management**

· Work with department and program leaders to clarify responsibilities, strengthen communication, and improve execution.

· Supervise assigned staff and support managers in setting expectations, addressing problems, and managing performance.

· Develop trust across the organization while maintaining clear leadership boundaries and accountability.

**Human Resources and Organizational Development**

· Support the relationship and services provided for Bethany House’s outsourced HR company.

· Help ensure that HR processes are timely, consistent, well documented, and compliant with applicable requirements.

**Financial and Administrative Operations**

· Work with the Executive Director and Director of Finance to connect operational decisions to budgets, staffing, funding requirements, and long-term sustainability.

· Monitor operational spending and help ensure that resources are used responsibly and within approved budgets.

· Support the development and consistent use of sound policies, procedures, and internal controls.

**Program, Shelter, Facilities, and Compliance Support**

· Maintain a working understanding of the operational needs of Bethany House’s shelters and programs and develop systems where needed.

· Work with staff and other stakeholders to resolve operational challenges.

· Be available when urgent operational issues arise, including unexpected events or leadership absences.

**Board Support and External Representation**

* Support the Executive Director in preparing presentations, reports, and other materials for the Board of Directors.
* Track Board decisions, action items, and organizational commitments to ensure timely follow-through.
* Oversee the maintenance of Board records, meeting minutes, and governance documentation to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with organizational requirements.

**Minimum Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

· Bachelor’s degree in business administration, nonprofit management, public administration, human services, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.

· Strong working knowledge of budgeting, human resources, compliance, organizational systems and project management.

· Demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgment, solve problems and manage complex projects through completion.

· Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, analytical and organizational skills.

· Experience in a regulated environment or nonprofit human services organization preferred.

· Proficiency with common office applications and project-management technology.

Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, community partners, and other stakeholders, the Director of Development will help build a sustainable and diversified fundraising program focused on major gifts, annual giving, corporate and foundation support, donor stewardship, special events and community engagement.

The Director will serve as a key ambassador for Bethany House, communicating the organization’s mission, impact, and funding needs to donors and community stakeholders and identifying opportunities to deepen philanthropic and community support.

* Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors.
* Strengthen annual giving and donor retention efforts.
* Develop and implement effective donor stewardship practices.

**Foundation & Corporate Giving**

* Use data and analytics to drive fundraising decisions.
* Oversee the tracking and acknowledgment of all donations and the development of fundraising campaign assets.

**Board & Leadership Partnership**

* Provide donor research, briefing materials, and strategic guidance.
* Foster a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.

SOUL RYEDERS is a Rye, New York-based 501(c)(3) public charity with a mission to provide personalized resources, innovative programs, and community support to anyone in the New York Tri-State area impacted by any type of cancer.

Through services including oncology social worker support, wellness programs, educational resources, support groups, wig exchange, and more, SOUL RYEDERS helps clients navigate every stage of a cancer diagnosis with dignity, confidence, hope, and compassion.

**Position Summary**

SOUL RYEDERS seeks an experienced, highly organized, and relationship-driven Director of Development to lead the execution of the organization's fundraising initiatives and sponsored events.

This individual will manage all aspects of development for the organization. The ideal candidate is experienced at cultivating sponsor and donor relationships, engaging new potential sponsors and donors, tracking fundraising progress, coordinating donor communications, and developing long-term relationships and systems to strengthen organizational growth through major donors, foundations and corporate support.

This role requires exceptional attention to detail, strong judgment, outstanding project management skills, and the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with staff, volunteers, donors, sponsors, and community partners.

* Produce, implement and advance SOUL RYEDERS' annual development plan.

* Lead all individual and major donor fundraising activities including identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship.
* Manage the planning and execution of fundraising campaigns and appeals.
* Manage all corporate sponsorship efforts including identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship.

* Create fundraising presentations, sponsorship materials, and donor-facing collateral using established style guide and/or deliver creative briefs to designers to develop required materials.

* Experience working with sponsorship programs and corporate partnerships.

jobs.description:
**DEPUTY DIRECTOR, PROCUREMENT (DACCO)**
========================================

* OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT

Posted on

10/01/2026

* Full-time

Location

BROOKLYN

* No exam required

Department

Office of the Chief Financial

Salary range: $94,203.00 – $99,940.00

Save

**Job Description**
-------------------

New York City Emergency Management (NYCEM) helps New Yorkers before, during, and after emergencies through preparedness, education, and response. NYCEM is responsible for coordinating citywide emergency planning and response for all types and scales of emergencies. We are staffed by more than 200 dedicated professionals with diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise, including individuals assigned from other City agencies.
  
  
The Office of the Chief Financial Officer is responsible for the oversight, management, accounting, and reporting of all agency funds, as well as the procurement planning, development, implementation, and management of all agency contracts.
  
The Procurement Unit is responsible for providing management, oversight, review, and support of all procurement functions at NYCEM. NYCEM procurements are governed by the City Charter and the City Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules.
  
  
Reporting to the Assistant Commissioner for Administration & Finance/ACCO, responsibilities include, but are not limited to: overseeing all contracting actions and vendor selection process, conferring with the ACCO and advising agency staff on appropriate procurement methodology and applicability of local procurement law, supervising procurement staff, reviewing solicitations and proposals, approving oversight documents such as pre-solicitation reports, recommendations for awards and request for renewals, and approving purchase orders and contracts in FMS.
  
  
The Deputy Agency Chief Contracting Officer (DACCO) will:
  

* Review and monitor agency procurement actions and contracting functions to ensure compliance with the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) rules and all other applicable city, state, and federal requirements.

  

* Oversee and manage procurements, varying in size and complexity, that focus on emergency events and citywide initiatives; ensure that multiple Program Unit needs are met in a timely manner; ensure that vendors understand Agency requirements and process flows.

  

* Approve Pre-Solicitation Report (PSRs), Recommendations for Award (RFAs), Responsibility Determinations (RDs) and other forms/information as required by the procurement process; oversee evaluation of submitted proposals; determine vendor responsiveness and responsibility; provide support in establishing and monitoring timelines for these tasks.

  

* Assist in drafting specifications/scopes of work; reviews and approves contract specifications before advertising to ensure conformity to the agency’s requirements and federal/state/city mandates; ensure proper content and format of Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and other solicitation documents.

  

* Monitor and update a variety of reports on the status of small and large-scale procurement plans for submission to oversight agencies.

  

* Approve requirements contract; purchase orders in FMS and/or PASSPort; submit contracts and task orders to the Comptroller’s Office for registration; track purchasing activity for management reporting and analysis.

  

* In the absence of the ACCO serve as the point of contact with the Mayor’s Office of Contract Services (MOCS); represent the agency at citywide ACCO meetings and relevant public hearings; research Division of Citywide Administrative Services (DCAS) requirements contracts and State/federal contracting opportunities; consult with other City agencies on best practices and recommended vendors.

  
\*\*PLEASE NOTE THE FOLLOWING:
  
  

* As part of NYCEM's emergency response mission, this position participates in an Emergency Operations Center (EOC) team. During emergency activations, team members may be required to work evenings, weekends, holidays, or extended shifts in support of City response operations. Outside of activations, EOC members participate in periodic training and exercises to maintain operational readiness, and must volunteer to assist with three Ready NY emergency preparedness presentations per year. EOC teams are on call for three weeks at a time, with six weeks off in between.

  

* Please note, the high end of the salary range is available to candidates who have been in City service two or more years.

  

* Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without employer support to be eligible for selection. Note that NYCEM does not participate in eVerify, which is required for the reauthorization of some visas.

This is an opportunity to join the senior leadership team of an agency committed to sharing the love of Jesus through dignified and compassionate care for poor and vulnerable neighbors of every faith and background, rooted in the Gospel and guided by the belief that every human life is sacred.

  

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the CPO will be a visible and influential member of the executive leadership team, responsible for ensuring that CCLI's ministries are operationally strong, financially sustainable, strategically aligned, and deeply rooted in the mission and teachings of the Catholic Church.

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy
jobs.description:
**Job Overview**

The Director of Philanthropy plays a key role in growing philanthropic revenue by implementing development strategies, cultivating relationships with individual, corporate, and foundation donors and partners, and coordinating fundraising events.

In partnership with the Chief Development Officer and Director of Operations, this role leads the Foundation’s fundraising efforts, developing a growth plan and building the team and infrastructure needed to execute it. The role leads donor identification and early-stage cultivation, using data and insights to identify opportunities and transition high-capacity donors to major gift portfolios. The position also cultivates foundation and corporate giving prospects and leads fundraising events.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, results-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities, translate strategy into action, and deliver measurable results. The candidate will have demonstrated success leading comprehensive fundraising programs in a healthcare setting, including direct experience leading and executing strategy in a major fundraising campaign.

This position serves as a key member of the Foundation’s leadership team, reports to the Chief Development Officer, and works closely with the Director of Operations and Board of Trustees.

**Responsibilities**

* Implement the organization’s annual fundraising plan with measurable goals and timelines.
* Cultivate and steward individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations, with a focus on donor acquisition, engagement, retention, and revenue growth.
* Grow the Foundation’s emerging grateful patient program by identifying, qualifying, and cultivating prospects to build a pipeline for major gifts.
* Develop funding proposals to match donor interests with University Hospital.
* Execute stewardship activities to retain and upgrade new and existing donors.
* Support annual, major, planned, and recurring giving strategies, including corporate and foundation fundraising beyond event sponsorships.
* Plan and execute fundraising events, such as the annual golf outing and cocktail-style event.
* Collaborate with staff, volunteers, and committees to meet event goals and enhance donor engagement.
* Serve as a member of the Foundation’s leadership team and work closely with CDO and Operations Director on strategic and tactical planning, forecasting, analysis, priority setting, and decision making to best position UHF in its efforts to support sustainable growth, particularly around major gifts.
* Strengthen collaboration between Foundation staff and University Hospital colleagues by promoting information sharing, cooperation, and a strong service orientation across the organization.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.
* Five (5) or more years of direct experience cultivating and stewarding donors in a healthcare setting and demonstrated success in individual, corporate, and foundation fundraising, donor portfolio management, and revenue growth.

· Demonstrated knowledge and experience developing and executing capital campaigns within a healthcare institution.

· Experience working effectively with senior executives, governing boards, volunteers, and other key stakeholders.

· Proficiency in CRM systems (knowledge of Salesforce a plus), Microsoft Office Suite, and reporting tools required; experience with campaign management platforms and donor analytics tools preferred.

**Core Competencies**

*Data-Driven Decision Making:* Uses donor data, reporting, and analytics to inform strategy, prioritize opportunities, and measure fundraising results.

*Relationship Building & Communication:* Builds and maintains strong relationships with donors, prospects, corporate partners, foundations, leadership, and cross-functional partners through effective written and verbal communication.

*Results Orientation:* Translates development strategies into action, prioritizes efforts effectively, and takes initiative to achieve measurable fundraising and revenue goals.

*Organization & Accountability:* Manages multiple priorities, maintains accurate and timely documentation, meets deadlines, and takes ownership of responsibilities with minimal supervision.

*Adaptability & Collaboration:* Thrives in a fast-paced environment, adapts to shifting priorities, and works collaboratively across the Foundation and Hospital to advance shared goals.

* Vision insurance

jobs.description:
A rare opportunity to define Aurora's next chapter, deepen its impact, and build the community support and resources to sustain it.

Aurora Day Camp creates joy, connection, and community for children with cancer and their siblings.

Aurora Day Camp seeks an accomplished, entrepreneurial Executive Director to lead the organization into its next decade. Working with Sunrise Association, the local Advisory Board, staff, families, and community partners, the Executive Director will strengthen Aurora's financial foundation, raise its visibility, deepen its year-round support for families, and build stronger relationships throughout Atlanta's pediatric cancer community.

Fundraising and financial sustainability will be central to the role. The Executive Director must be a credible and effective fundraiser who can build relationships, broaden community support, and secure the resources required to carry out Aurora's priorities. This leader must also connect fundraising to a broader vision for mission impact, family engagement, strong partnerships, and organizational excellence.

**About Aurora Day Camp**

Aurora Day Camp brings back the simple joys of childhood for children with cancer and their siblings. Through a six- week summer day camp, year-round programs, and Aurora on Wheels in-hospital activities, children can play, create, build friendships, and simply be kids. Every program is offered free of charge to families.

Now entering its tenth year, Aurora has become a valued part of Atlanta's pediatric cancer community. The organization works alongside families, healthcare providers, volunteers, donors, foundations, and community partners across the region. Aurora is locally led and supported, with a seasoned Camp Director providing experienced leadership for camp and program delivery.

The Sunrise Association is both Aurora's fiscal sponsor and an important organizational partner. Sunrise provides financial administration, accreditation support, insurance, operational guidance, and access to a larger cohort of day camps serving children with cancer and their siblings across the United States and around the world. This partnership gives Aurora the benefits of established infrastructure and shared expertise while allowing it to remain deeply rooted in the Atlanta community.

**The Opportunity**

Aurora has built a strong programmatic foundation and is ready to define its next chapter. The next Executive Director will help determine where Aurora should be in three to five years and what partnerships, staffing, volunteer leadership, systems, visibility, and financial resources will be needed to deepen its impact. The opportunity is not simply to grow the number of campers. It is to make Aurora better known and supported, strengthen year-round

connections with families, deepen collaboration with Children's Healthcare of Atlanta and other pediatric cancer organizations, and establish Aurora as an essential part of Atlanta's pediatric cancer community.

This is an entrepreneurial role in a lean, approximately $1 million organization. The successful candidate will be both strategic and hands-on, equally comfortable facilitating a planning conversation, developing board leadership,

meeting with a major donor, reviewing a budget, representing Aurora in the community, and helping the team solve an immediate problem.

The Executive Director will report to Sunrise Association and work closely with Aurora's local Advisory Board. The Executive Director will directly supervise and work closely with the Camp Director. The role offers meaningful local leadership and autonomy along with the resources and accountability of a larger partner organization.

**What the Executive Director Will Lead**

**Fundraising and Financial Sustainability**

* Serve as Aurora's chief fundraiser and personally manage a portfolio of individual, corporate, and foundation prospects and donors.
* Develop and execute a diversified, multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with Aurora's strategic priorities.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors, sponsors, foundations, and corporate partners throughout Greater Atlanta.
* Lead grant strategy, proposal development, reporting, and relationship management.
* Provide leadership for Aurora's signature fundraising efforts, including the Dare to Dream Gala, AuroraWALKS, and other community events.
* Equip Advisory Board members, volunteers, and staff to succeed as ambassadors, relationship builders, and fundraising partners.

**Vision Strategy and Mission Impact**

* Partner with Sunrise Association, the Advisory Board, staff, families, and community stakeholders to articulate a compelling vision for Aurora's next decade.
* Develop and execute a practical three-to-five-year strategic roadmap with clear priorities, measurable objectives, and the resources required for success.
* Identify opportunities to deepen Aurora's support for families beyond camp, strengthen community awareness, and expand collaboration across Atlanta's pediatric cancer community.

**Board and Organizational Leadership**

* Strengthen the Advisory Board as a strategic leadership body by clarifying expectations, deepening engagement, and recruiting members whose skills, relationships, and perspectives advance Aurora's mission.
* Translate strategy into annual priorities, budgets, work plans, accountability, and measurable results.
* Directly supervise and support the Camp Director and coordinate effectively with the broader Aurora team.
* Strengthen organizational systems and oversee financial performance, budgeting, compliance, and administration in close partnership with Sunrise Association's finance and operational teams.

**Team Leadership and Culture**

* Sustain Aurora's positive, mission-centered culture and create an environment in which staff members feel supported, valued, accountable, and connected to shared priorities.
* Lead and coordinate a small team whose members bring distinct areas of expert

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and operation of New Horizons Healthcare, a Federally Qualified Health Center. The CEO works collaboratively with the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership team to establish organizational priorities, implement strategic initiatives, oversee resources, and ensure the delivery of high-quality, accessible healthcare services to the communities served.

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization in alignment with its mission and Board-approved goals.
* Partner with the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership team to establish priorities, implement strategies, and evaluate organizational performance.
* Oversee financial, clinical, operational, administrative, and workforce functions to ensure organizational effectiveness and sustainability.

* Maintain strong relationships with community partners, government agencies, funders, and other stakeholders.

**Education and Experience**

* Minimum of seven (7) years of senior-level leadership experience in a nonprofit healthcare or human services organization.
* Demonstrated experience leading organizational operations, personnel, healthcare programs, and budgets.
* Community Health Center or Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) experience highly desirable.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong executive leadership, strategic planning, financial management, and decision-making skills.

This position is onsite and requires regular interaction with employees, the Board of Directors, patients, community partners, government representatives, and other external stakeholders.

New Horizons Healthcare is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Through its mission, the Ohio Children's Alliance fosters a brighter future for Ohio's children and families through advocacy, innovation, and collaboration with health and human services organizations.

**Seeking an Executive Director**

The Bay School Community Arts Center

Mathews, Virginia

Lead. Inspire. Connect. Create.

The Bay School Community Arts Center is seeking an enthusiastic, creative, and community-minded Executive Director to lead our nonprofit community arts center in Mathews, Virginia.

For more than 20 years, the Bay School has provided opportunities for people of all ages to experience, learn, create, and connect through the arts. Our center includes a gallery, art classes and workshops, summer art camps, community outreach programs, special events, and a pottery studio. Chicago Public Media is one of the nation's largest local nonprofit news organizations. Home to WBEZ 91.5FM, the Chicago Sun-Times, and Vocalo. As a mission-driven organization, we aspire to be the most trusted news source Chicagoans turn to for understanding the people, events, and ideas shaping our community.

**Description**
---------------

Under the direction of the City Administrator, Deputy Executive Director (DED) provides operational, financial, and administrative leadership of the Housing and Redevelopment Authority (HRA) while ensuring full regulatory compliance and organizational excellence.? This position oversees the day-to-day operation of the HRA by ensuring effective implementation of the policies, priorities, and goals set forth by the City Administrator. ?
  
  
The Deputy Executive Director is responsible for developing and leading a high-performing team in a collaborative and supportive environment and delivering measurable community impact.? The Deputy Executive Director works with the City Administrator, community stakeholders, public officials and staff to ensure the HRA succeeds in providing safe, affordable, quality housing with excellence, and in compliance with HUD requirements, Minnesota statutes, Dakota County CDA requirements, MHFA program requirements, fair housing laws, and other applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

**Examples of Duties**
----------------------

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
  
*Direct Oversight Supervision:* Housing Programs Administrator, Property Managers, Housing Office Specialist, Maintenance Staff, Cleaner/Caretaker Staff
  
*Indirect Supervision:* Temporary Employees, Assigned Contractors and Consultants
  
  
**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
  
The Deputy Executive Director position is a highly responsible, professional, supervisory, and administrative leadership position within the HRA. The Deputy Executive Director exercises significant discretion and performs a broad range of duties relating to the successful oversight of HRA capital improvements, asset management, regulatory compliance, day-to-day operations, administration, and management of the Housing Authority including but not limited to:

* Oversee the management, planning, and general direction of the HRA.
* Recommend new hires; train, supervise, evaluate staff performance; recommend promotions and terminations of employment.
* Draft HRA budgets for the City Administrator approval and administer HRA budgets once approved.
* Prepare records, files, and reports. Analyze data and prepare recommendations for City Administrator action.
* Advise the City Administrator in developing and recommending HRA policies and programmatic actions.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Establish departmental priorities, annual work plans, performance expectations, and benchmarks.
* Oversight of assignments and execution of work ensuring staff accountability, operational effectiveness, and alignment with organizational goals and objectives.

* In the absence of the Executive Director (City Administrator), the Deputy Director represents the Housing Authority in meetings with partner agencies, makes public appearances, and communicates with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.

This position is responsible for all administrative tasks associated with the Divisions. The Regional ED (Executive Director) will work alongside the volunteer President and Division Board of Directors. The Regional ED will serve as a liaison to the RSPA network on a national, divisional, and regional level and to the divisional committees.  
  
This position will be full-time, requiring 40 hours per week, with approximately 2–4 traveling weekends per year. The Regional ED will be required to participate in divisional board meetings, conference calls, the April Executive Committee meeting, divisional conventions, workshops, one-day events, the World Conference in September, and other RSPA meetings and events as needed. These commitments may be held virtually or in person and may occasionally require evening or weekend availability.

The Regional Executive Director is an employee of the RSPA National Office. This individual will report to the RSPA CEO and work alongside volunteer Division Presidents and Regional Vice Presidents of their assigned divisions.

**Essential Functions**:

* Membership Development & Outreach:
  + Lead strategies and initiatives to attract, onboard and retain members
  + Respond to all member emails and phone calls in a timely fashion
  + Follow up with applicants in the pipeline to assist them in getting registered for workshops, division events, etc.
  + Supervise, coordinate and implement all facets of membership development with the board
  + Work closely with the coach developers within division to schedule workshops, publish a full year calendar and promote attendance in workshops
  + Generate membership reports using RSPA Divisions Dashboard. Use reports to keep track of membership numbers and finding ways to reach out to applicants, certified members, retired, etc.
  + Support National Membership department during dues renewal by answering questions new members may have, reaching out to outstanding members and using resources to find new members
* Regional Events & Member Engagement:
  + Plan and execute a calendar of regional, one-day member events in partnership with divisional volunteer leadership
  + Manage event logistics, including venues, contracts, catering, speakers, registration, travel, and on-site execution
  + Coordinate event marketing and communications with the National Marketing team, including email, social media, and promotional materials

jobs.description:
**JOB TITLE:** Director of Development & External Affairs

**DEPARTMENT:** M&G

**EDUCATION LEVEL:** 4 Year Degree

**REPORTS TO:** CEO

**TRAVEL:** Occasional local travel may be required

**FLSA STATUS:** Exempt

**SUPERVISORY ROLE:** Yes

**ABOUT ACCESSHEALTH**

AccessHealth is a private, not-for-profit Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) serving Fort Bend and Waller Counties, TX since 1975 providing integrated, affordable healthcare to ~20,000 patients annually across 17 locations. A 2025 HRSA National Quality Leader and NCQA Patient-Centered Medical Home.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Director of Development & External Affairs leads AccessHealth’s fundraising, external partnerships, community engagement, and strategic communications efforts. The position is responsible for expanding philanthropic support, strengthening community and referral partnerships, and increasing AccessHealth’s visibility throughout the communities it serves.

Working closely with the CEO and organizational leadership, the Director develops and executes strategies that strengthen AccessHealth’s financial sustainability, community presence, and relationships with donors, corporations, foundations, healthcare organizations, government stakeholders, and community partners.

**ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Fundraising, Donor Development & Events**

* Develop and execute AccessHealth’s annual fundraising and development strategy.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward individual donors, corporate partners, foundations, and other philanthropic supporters.
* Manage donor development activities from prospect identification through solicitation and stewardship.
* Identify and pursue grant opportunities and oversee grant development, submission, reporting, and compliance.
* Plan and oversee fundraising campaigns, sponsorship opportunities, donor engagement activities, and signature fundraising events.
* Develop strategies to increase donor retention, recurring giving, corporate sponsorships, and philanthropic revenue.
* Maintain accurate donor and fundraising records within the organization’s CRM or donor management system.
* Establish fundraising goals and provide regular development reports to the CEO and Board of Directors.
* Support the Board Development Committee and related development initiatives.

**Strategic Partnerships & External Affairs**

* Develop and maintain strategic relationships with hospitals, healthcare organizations, employers, schools, faith-based organizations, nonprofits, and other community partners.
* Identify partnership opportunities that increase awareness of AccessHealth services and strengthen appropriate patient referral pathways.
* Build and maintain relationships with government officials, community leaders, and other key stakeholders in coordination with the CEO.
* Represent AccessHealth at chambers of commerce, community coalitions, healthcare forums, and other external meetings and events.
* Monitor community needs and external trends and identify opportunities that support AccessHealth’s mission and strategic priorities.

**Communications, Brand & Digital Strategy**

* Oversee external communications and marketing initiatives that strengthen awareness of AccessHealth’s services, programs, impact, and mission.
* Direct digital marketing and search visibility strategies, including SEO, social media, website visibility, and emerging AI-driven search technologies.
* Coordinate media relations, public announcements, and external communications in collaboration with the CEO and organizational leadership.
* Oversee the development of impact reports, donor communications, community materials, and other external-facing publications.
* Monitor marketing and engagement performance and recommend strategies to strengthen AccessHealth’s external reach and visibility.

**Leadership & Administration**

* Serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO on fundraising, external partnerships, community engagement, and development opportunities.
* Establish and monitor goals and key performance indicators for development and external affairs activities.
* Develop and manage applicable departmental budgets and resources.
* Collaborate across departments to ensure development and external affairs initiatives align with organizational priorities.
* Perform other duties and special projects as assigned by the Chief Executive Officer.

**EDUCATION/LICENSURE/CERTIFICATION QUALIFICATIONS:**

**REQUIRED:**

* 7+ years in nonprofit development, healthcare business development, or comparable external-facing leadership
* Proven track record: personally closed gifts, grants, or sponsorships of $25,000+; managed an annual fund of $500,000+
* Experience producing fundraising events generating $100,000+ in revenue
* Grant writing and management (federal, state, and/or private foundation)
* Proficiency in CRM/donor software (Bloomerang, DonorPerfect, Salesforce, Raiser's Edge, or equivalent)
* Working knowledge of SEO, digital marketing, and social media
* Brings an established network in Greater Houston / Fort Bend County - foundation contacts, hospital community benefit leaders, corporate giving relationships. Day-one relationships matter.
* Genuine commitment to health equity and serving underserved communities

**PREFERRED:**

* Master's degree (MPH, MBA, MPA, MHA) or CFRE certification
* FQHC or safety-net healthcare experience
* AIO/LLM search optimization experience

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Provides leadership and oversight to assigned staff, contractors, vendors, or other resources supporting development, communications, community engagement, fundraising, and external affairs activities, as applicable. Responsibilities may include work assignment, performance oversight, coaching, and coordination of departmental priorities.
