All candidate nominations, referrals, and inquiries regarding this opportunity should be directed to:  
  
Melissa Estevez Executive Search Consultant, LHH Executive Search Melissa.Estevez@lhh.com | 617-313-8320  
  
Megan McQuay Partner, Executive Search, LHH Executive Search Megan.Mcquay@lhh.com | 505-348-2982  
  
Confidential inquiries are welcomed.  
  
To be considered for this role, please provide your inquiry to LHH no later than October 15, 2026  
  
The CEO of CNM Ingenuity is the senior executive of the organization, accountable to the CNM Ingenuity Board of Directors for the strategic direction, operational performance, financial health, and mission integrity of the organization. Working collaboratively with the College President, the CEO ensures that CNM Ingenuity's strategy, pillars of work, and administrative practices align with and further the College's mission and extend a culture of innovation to the benefit of the College, the region, and the state.  
  
This is a leadership role rather than a hands-on role across every function. The CEO leads through a senior team and is expected to build, develop, and hold accountable the functional leadership required across real estate, finance, contracts and managed services, programs, external relations, and operations. The CEO operates with significant executive authority and is expected to bring entrepreneurial energy, industry fluency, and governance experience to the role.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**THE CNM ENTERPRISE**

Formed in 1965, Central New Mexico Community College (the College) is a public college created by statute and governed by an elected Governing Board. It is the largest undergraduate institution in New Mexico. In the most recent federal comparison cited by the College, CNM ranked first nationally for associate degrees and certificates earned by Hispanic learners, first for credentials earned by Native American learners, and second for the total number awarded by a community college.

The College enterprise includes three component organizations, each distinct yet related, and all within the “One CNM” brand:

* **CNM Ingenuity, Inc.:** a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation formed in 2014 under the New Mexico University Research Park and Economic Development Act (NMSA 1978, Chapter 21, Article 28). The Act provides a framework to create corporations that advance education, science, research, conservation, health care, and economic development.
* **The CNM Foundation:** a 501(c)(3) charitable organization that receives donations and gifts for the College enterprise, including CNM Ingenuity.
* **CNM Holdings, Inc.:** a for-profit corporation that holds title to most residential and commercial real estate purchased for the purpose of diversifying enterprise assets, among other things.

Together, these component organizations help the CNM enterprise remain resilient and responsive during a challenging period for higher education. Filings and annual audits are available through the New Mexico Office of the State Auditor.

**ABOUT CNM INGENUITY**

CNM Ingenuity serves as the College's innovation, economic diversification, and workforce development entity. It works with private and public partners to identify, test, implement, and scale entrepreneurial and statewide economic development opportunities, drawing on organizational and

cultural strengths distinct from those of the College itself. CNM Ingenuity revenues support the College's mission.

The majority of CNM Ingenuity's revenue-generating activity lies outside of programming. CNM Ingenuity manages two significant multi-year State contracts, including a $16.7 million agreement with the New Mexico Early Childhood Education and Care Department and a $22.0 million agreement with the New Mexico Public Education Department. It manages the College enterprise's most versatile investment fund, currently more than $20 million. It also manages commercial and residential real estate holdings and substantial short-term and long-term leasing of College properties. These activities are designed primarily to generate alternative revenues in support of the College's mission and to serve economic and community development goals.

CNM Ingenuity also serves as a test bed for responsive programming and for alternative models of delivering education and training, developed quickly and then scaled using the College's resources and systems. Its portfolio is organized around four pillars: real estate; entrepreneurship; managed services for State agencies and others; and workforce and contract training. Programs include accelerated skills training, deep technology workforce development, entrepreneurship support, venture fund management, and space solutions.

CNM Ingenuity's work is shaped by the needs of New Mexico's employers and learners, and those needs evolve. Current efforts support State and regional priorities in the quantum, sustainable energy, aerospace, and national security sectors and their supporting industries. The next CEO should expect these priorities to change over time and will be responsible for positioning CNM Ingenuity to move with them.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

This is a transitional moment for CNM Ingenuity, and the next CEO is being asked to lead through it. The organization has grown from a research park with a handful of programs into a multifaceted innovation enterprise, and its structure now needs to catch up with its scale.

The next CEO will develop CNM Ingenuity's structure, policies, and practices so that the organ

jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
Bartram’s Garden seeks a full-time Director of Development to oversee all fundraising activities within a strong and successful team. The Director of Development reports to the Chief Advancement & Experience Officer, who previously held this role, and serves the Bartram’s Garden mission through all aspects of contributed income, including both operational and capital fundraising.

As a dynamic and values-driven non-profit, Bartram’s Garden generates roughly $4–5 million in contributed income each year to support ongoing operations, programming, and special projects. The Garden is also in the midst of a multi-year, multi-million-dollar capital campaign to support major campus investments and the organization’s long-term sustainability. In a sign of the organization’s fundraising prowess and strong reputation among regional and local philanthropists, elected officials, and partners, the first phase of the campus plan is projected for completion in 2028—perfectly timed to align with the 300th anniversary of the Garden’s founding.

The Bartram’s Garden Director of Development is responsible for leading and implementing the fundraising programs for Bartram’s Garden with efficiency, a goal-oriented mindset, and clear alignment with both the Garden’s strategic plan and the mission, vision, and values.

Responsibilities:

*Fundraising*

· Work closely with the Chief Advancement & Experience Officer to plan and oversee all fundraising for the organization, with operational goals of at least $4–$5M annually

· Cultivate, secure, and manage new and renewing sources of support with an emphasis on diversified revenue streams, including grants from private foundations, corporate sponsors, awards from public sources (city, state, and federal), and individual giving, including major and planned gifts

· Play a lead role in developing and implementing the campaign associated with the Garden’s 300th anniversary in 2028, with a focus on advancing the strategic plan and growing the endowment

· Drive the success of longer-term campaigns and project-specific fundraising, including capital investments, by developing cases for support, meeting with or supporting meetings with donors, managing donor stewardship and naming opportunities, and facilitating prospect research

· Oversee the management and coordination of all galas and cultivation events for the organization, including event planning, solicitation of sponsorships from individuals and corporations, and outreach to honorees and stakeholders

*Supervision & Department Management*

· Oversee, train, and assess the Development Manager, Development Coordinator, and any consultants

· Lead and model effective, timely, and mission-aligned funder stewardship through relationship cultivation, reporting, and other outreach

· Manage and evaluate internal systems, vendors, and tools, such as CRM software and tracking practices

· Support staff from all departments to deepen capacity for fundraising and donor relations as a component of effective public space and program management

· Collaborate with the Advancement & Experience team to ensure that site-wide visitor experience drives increased contributed revenue through strategies such as messaging, signage, staffed interactions, and more

*Strategy & Planning*

· With input from the Executive Team and Development department, create the annual fundraising plan in coordination with the Garden’s strategic initiatives as well as annual goals

· In coordination with the Development and Finance teams, provide timely and accurate budget projections towards both operating and project-specific goals

· Identify potential barriers and challenges to meeting revenue goals and collaboratively implement strategies to overcome these issues

· Share progress updates in writing and verbally with key stakeholders, including our Board of Trustees, Executive Team, and staff

· Facilitate the Board of Director’s Advancement Committee through preparing agendas and materials, capturing notes and action items, and working closely with the committee chair to advance the board’s engagement in fundraising

· Oversee development and update of policies for gift acceptance, donor recognition, and similar

Qualifications and Requirements

· 7+ years of experience and demonstrated success in non-profit fundraising, with at least some in a leadership role. The ideal candidate will have proven success in securing and managing at least two the following:

· Major individual gifts ($100K+)

· Multi-year foundation support

· State or federal grants

· Planned gifts

· Fundraising campaigns in support of capital investments, endowment growth, or other targeted initiatives

· Demonstrated ability to supervise and manage staff and consultants.

· Excellent communication skills. Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively communicate with staff, visitors, and donors from diverse backgrounds in terms of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, class, and religion.

· Strong writing skills with an ability to prepare thought-provoking, compelling, and timely proposals, reports, responses, and pitches on a range of subjects for varying audiences.

· Comfortable engaging stakeholders over the phone, via email, and in person.

· Confident making projections and analyzing data.

· Proficient reading, interpreting, and talking about budgets.

· Experience using a customer relationship management platform to input and track data.

· Organized, detail-driven, and willing to take initiative.

· Exemplary time management skills and able to manage multiple competing priorities and deadlines effectively without close supervision.

· Ability to navigate and assess varied online and technological resources independently.

**Organization Overview**

**Founded in 1951 by Corning Incorporated as a gift to the nation, the Corning Museum of Glass (CMoG) is the global center for the art, science, and history of glass.** The Museum shapes the understanding and appreciation of glass worldwide and draws more than 300,000 visitors each year to a city of roughly 10,000 residents. The *New York Times* named CMoG as one of the U.S. museums to see in 2025, and *Newsweek* readers voted CMoG one of the Top 3 Best Art Museums in America.

With more than 10,000 works on display, the Museum galleries showcase glass selected from a permanent collection of more than 50,000 objects representing more than 3,500 years of history. The expansive collection is presented in three core galleries – 35 Centuries of Glass, Heineman, and Contemporary Art & Design – to tell the global story of glass from antiquity through the present day. The Innovation Galleries highlight scientific and technological achievements using glass, ranging from casserole dishes to telescopes to optical fiber.

**CMoG is regarded as the conservation authority on glass to museums and institutions around the world.**

In late 2024, the Museum celebrated the expansion of The Studio, funded primarily by a successful capital campaign. The Studio, which is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, features the first large scale kiln casting facility in North America and can support over 100,000 Make Your Own Glass projects annually. The state-of-the-art facilities provide artists and students with the tools and the support they need to take risks and make discoveries; opportunities for people of all skill levels to forge and deepen their understanding of glass; and connections to the glass community, where artists gather to create, learn, and share.

**Role Summary & Context for Recruitment**

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is responsible for the strategic planning, management, and success of the comprehensive fundraising efforts of the Corning Museum of Glass, including the pursuit of long-term relationships that benefit the financial health of the Museum. The CDO oversees policy, strategy, and execution of the work of the Development Department, which includes individual and planned giving, corporate, foundation and government giving, membership, giving appeals, special events, and donor relations programs. This leader reports to the Museum President and Executive Director, providing them with expert advice on all aspects of fundraising, including policy development and changes as well as new program directions. The CDO will manage all future campaigns. The CDO works closely with the Development Committee and Board of Trustees to build the Museum’s visibility, impact, and financial resources. The CDO serves as a champion for CMoG and the catalyst in strengthening the Museum’s culture of philanthropy.

The CDO oversees a team of seven staff members and provides strategic oversight and leadership for the Development Department’s annual operating budget.

Formal fundraising at CMoG is a relatively young discipline, having taken shape over the past decade alongside the Museum's landmark expansion of The Studio, and its successful capital campaign. As CMoG enters its next chapter, the Museum is investing in building a comprehensive, professionalized development program capable of matching the global stature of its collection, scholarship, and artistic community. The CDO will have the rare opportunity to help shape this program's strategy, systems, and team at an early and formative stage of its growth.

The CDO will be a close strategic partner and an active member of the Museum's leadership team. This is an opportunity to help shape CMoG's comprehensive strategic and fundraising plan, to be developed in partnership with the President and Board of Trustees over the coming year.

With a world-renowned glass collection, the preeminent Rakow Research Library, and a thriving community of working studio artists, CMoG offers an unusually rich philanthropic story. The CDO will have the opportunity to build Development’s presence among collector, scholarly, and design communities nationally and internationally, while deepening engagement with members and visitors closer to home.

CMoG will consider a broad range of backgrounds. The ideal candidate will align with the following qualifications:

* Minimum of 10 years of successful nonprofit fundraising with a track record of increased managerial responsibility and fundraising success.
* Demonstrated track record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and securing significant major gifts, coupled with experience leading and developing successful fundraising teams.
* Demonstrated experience securing corporate philanthropic support and foundation and government grants.

* Demonstrated experience utilizing modern fundraising databases, data analytics, and AI-enabled tools and techniques to identify and qualify prospective donors, strengthen fundraising strategies, and improve donor engagement and fundraising effectiveness.
* Possesses a global orientation and knowledge of strategies and trends in global philanthropy.

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

**Location:** Orange, Osceola, and Seminole Counties, Florida

**Position Overview**

Want to lead a program where strong operations and strong relationships can genuinely change lives?

The Transition House, Inc. is seeking a collaborative, mission-driven Program Director to lead our Veteran Connection and Suicide Prevention Program. Funded through the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program, this community-based program helps Veterans and other eligible individuals connect with critical support before challenges become crises.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can turn a grant-funded vision into consistent, responsive services. You will guide a multidisciplinary team, strengthen partnerships with the VA and community providers, monitor program quality and performance, and make sure Veterans receive timely, respectful, and well-coordinated support.

The program primarily provides non-clinical suicide-prevention services to individuals who may be experiencing suicide risk or significant life stressors, including homelessness, housing instability, unemployment, financial hardship, justice involvement, behavioral health or substance-use concerns, family stress, social isolation, and disconnection from VA care.

**Why Join The Transition House**

At The Transition House, we believe strong teams create strong outcomes. Our work is centered on accountability, rehabilitation, and creating opportunities for individuals working toward stability and a stronger future.

**Veterans Community Project (VCP) Overview**

VCP was founded in Kansas City, Missouri, in 2016 by a group of combat Veterans shaped by their military service and began with a determination to do better for Veterans in need. Today, we’re growing nationwide to serve more Veterans everywhere, ensuring no one is left behind. Our founders’ solution was simple: provide Veterans experiencing homelessness with a home of their own and wraparound case management services that leverage the support of the community to not only get them back on their feet, but ensure they continue standing. Our proven model has an 85% success rate at getting Veterans back on their feet.

**The Team**

We, the team members and co-founders of VCP, operate with innovation, entrepreneurism, and grit in our mission to serve those who served. We move with swift, bold action, driven by purpose. We believe in collaboration, community, compassion, and above all, serving Veterans with dignity and respect. We serve all Veterans with that ethos—regardless of length or type of service, or discharge status.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Major Gifts will build and manage a diverse portfolio of individual, family, foundation, corporate, and other philanthropic prospects to advance Veterans Community Project's mission to fix Veteran homelessness. VCP operates as a network of Villages nationwide, each supported locally, alongside a Central Services Team (CST) that provides the shared infrastructure, systems, and support that keep every Village running. While VCP is a $20 million organization, this role is dedicated specifically to securing unrestricted, capacity-building, and strategic gifts for CST, which operates on an approximate $3 million budget separate from site-level fundraising, with the support of other CST team members. * Support national fundraising campaigns and special initiatives as assigned.

* Experience building and scaling a major-gift portfolio or prospect pipeline, rather than solely managing an established one.

In addition to a competitive compensation package, ACEH provides **comprehensive health benefits** and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on one of Anchorage's most important community priorities.

· Advance ACEH's strategic vision and community impact

**Executive Director, Private Foundation**

**Location:** Pensacola, Florida I On-Site **Employment:** Full-Time, Exempt **Reports to:** Board of Directors

-------------------

Covenant Health and Community Services is a private grantmaking foundation focused on improving health and well-being across generations in Northwest Florida. Initial priorities include aging, behavioral health, and access to care.

The Executive Director will serve as the Foundation's chief executive and principal partner to the Board during a formative stage of development. This leader will help shape strategy, build the operating model and grantmaking approach, and position Covenant for lasting community impact.

------------------------

**Board Partnership & Governance**

* Serve as the Board's principal executive partner and trusted advisor on strategy, grantmaking, financial stewardship, governance, risk, and long-term sustainability.

**Strategy & Organizational Leadership**
----------------------------------------

* Set and lead organizational strategy and operations in alignment with Covenant's mission, community priorities, and Board direction.

----------------------------------

**Assistant Director of Development**

*Linfield University is seeking a relationship-driven and motivated fundraising professional to join University Advancement as Assistant Director of Development. This role offers the opportunity to build meaningful connections with donors, advance philanthropic support, and help strengthen the University’s mission through thoughtful engagement and stewardship.*

**Job Description**

**Title:** Assistant Director of Development

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Reports To:** Associate Vice President for Development

**FTE:** 1.0

**Department:** University Advancement

**Effective Date:** September, 2026

**Job Summary:**

The Assistant Director of Development (AsstDOD) is an externally facing position that is responsible for the qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of prospective and current donors to Linfield University in an effort to advance Linfield’s mission and goals. The AsstDOD works as a generalist, with a focus of activity on mid-level gifts ($1,000 - $10,000). The AsstDOD is expected to initiate contact with potential donors, develop and implement appropriate solicitation plans and strategies, and involve other members of the university community as appropriate. This is all done in a donor-centered manner by linking the interests and passions of a donor with needs of the University. Frequent travel and occasional evening and weekend work is required to be successful in this position, as are highly developed communication skills, tact, diplomacy and excellent judgment.

**Responsibilities:**

* Manage a portfolio of roughly 200 donor prospects to qualify, cultivate, solicit and steward gifts to Linfield, particularly in the range of $1,000 - $10,000. This work is done using a variety of methods and tools, including email, social media, in-person and virtual one-on-one meetings.
* Meet annual metrics relating to specific numbers of people making gifts in the $1,000 - $10,000 range, including donors new to that level of giving, donors that increase within that level, and donors that renew at that level after not doing so for several years.
* When appropriate, develop and implement plans to yield more significant philanthropic support, whether through an outright major gift or a documented deferred gift commitment.
* Collaborate with other members of the Advancement team to coordinate and complete special fundraising projects proposed by various departments of the University.
* Maintain accurate records of contacts with donors and prospects and ensure that all activity is recorded in the Advancement database (Salesforce).
* Develop partnerships with faculty and other university staff that provide opportunities for donors and prospects to learn about aspects of the university that would best align with their interests/passions.
* Ensure appropriate stewardship plans are prepared, and activities conducted, for donors.
* Demonstrate integrity, self-confidence, decisiveness, diplomacy, determination, intellectual curiosity and a passion for building a culture of philanthropy at Linfield.
* Provide regular reports of activities to demonstrate progress toward established goals.
* Perform other duties as assigned including following all University policies and procedures.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of two years of experience in development/fundraising, marketing, or sales.
* Ability to create authentic and meaningful relationships with alumni, donors, administrators, faculty, and students that lead to increased support of the University.
* Strong verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
* Passion for higher education, and in particular, the experience provided by a small private university in the liberal arts tradition.
* Ability to collaborate as a member of a strong, goal-directed team.
* Superior organizational skills.
* Ability to take initiative in managing projects and timelines with minimal supervision.
* Working knowledge of fundraising databases (preferably Salesforce), Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
* Ability to handle confidential donor information with tact and discretion.
* Availability to work evenings and weekends to attend events and fundraising visits on and off campus.
* Must have valid driver's license and be able to conduct occasional overnight travel.

**If you are passionate about building meaningful relationships, advancing higher education, and helping grow a culture of philanthropy, we encourage you to apply and consider joining the Linfield University Advancement team.**

**Linfield University participates in E-Verify to verify the identity and work eligibility of all new employees.**

**To apply, please submit your application materials through the Linfield University employment portal. We look forward to learning more about how your experience and passion align with our mission.**

* Monitor legislation, budgets, and policy developments affecting Kansas higher education and provide timely analysis and recommendations.
* Facilitate information sharing, coordinated planning, and consistent messaging with system partners around Board-approved legislative, budget, and policy priorities.
* Prepare briefings, testimony, talking points, reports, and other materials for senior leadership and the Board.
* Represent KBOR in legislative, governmental, public policy, and higher education forums.

**Preferred Candidate Profile**

The successful candidate will bring significant experience in government relations, legislative affairs, public policy, or a closely related field; strong knowledge of Kansas legislative and budget processes; exceptional communication and relationship-building skills; and demonstrated ability to exercise political judgment and influence without direct authority. * Experience advising senior executive leadership on legislative, policy, budgetary, governmental, or stakeholder strategy.

* Demonstrated ability to build consensus, influence senior leaders and policymakers, and achieve results through collaboration and relationship-based leadership.

Assistant Director of Development and Affinity Engagement

**Department:**

Advancement | Alumni Association

**Position Overview**

The Assistant Director of Development and Affinity Engagement advances The Ohio State University’s philanthropic priorities by managing leadership annual giving relationships and using alumni and affinity engagement as a strategic pathway for donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and pipeline development. This hybrid position is primarily focused on cultivating and soliciting leadership annual gifts of $3,000 to $99,999, while also strengthening alumni and constituent relationships through engagement strategies that support fundraising outcomes and Advancement priorities. As a member of the Connections team within the Ohio State University Alumni Association (OSUAA), the Assistant Director proactively manages an assigned portfolio of leadership annual giving donors and prospects through in-person visits, virtual outreach, engagement opportunities, and targeted cultivation activity. The role emphasizes discovery, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of donors, identification and referral of future major gift prospects, and collaboration with volunteers and alumni leaders to advance fundraising and engagement strategies. The primary audiences for the Assistant Director include OSUAA affinity groups and Buckeye Connected Communities, with engagement activity intentionally focused on strengthening donor relationships, identifying prospective philanthropic support, and advancing leadership annual giving outcomes.

  
  

In addition to direct fundraising responsibilities, the Assistant Director serves as a liaison to select affinity groups and Buckeye Connected Communities to support engagement strategies that deepen constituent relationships and create opportunities for donor cultivation, stewardship, and pipeline development. The position also contributes to the development, execution, and evaluation of engagement programs and communications within assigned audiences or regions, ensuring those activities support Advancement priorities, donor engagement, and leadership annual giving objectives. This role requires frequent travel, including approximately two overnight trips per month, evening and weekend work, and the ability to monitor and administer an allocated budget in alignment with Advancement policies and fiscal guidelines. Success is measured through established fundraising and engagement metrics, including donor meetings, qualifications, solicitations, dollars raised, major gift referrals, first-time event attendees, and increased volunteer participation.

  
  

Reporting to the Senior Director of Buckeye Connected Communities, the Assistant Director operates with independence and professional judgment in managing assigned donor portfolios and engagement activities within established Advancement strategies, fundraising goals, policies, and performance expectations. Strong interpersonal, organizational, and analytical skills are essential, along with the ability to manage donor relationships, interpret engagement and fundraising opportunities, adapt to shifting priorities, and collaborate across Advancement and university departments.

Alfred State College seeks a dynamic, relationship-centered, and forward-thinking Executive Director of Admissions to provide strategic leadership for undergraduate admissions and recruitment.

Reporting to the Vice President for Enrollment Management, the Executive Director will lead a talented admissions team responsible for attracting, recruiting, admitting, and enrolling students who will thrive at Alfred State. The successful candidate will build upon recent enrollment momentum while helping the College evolve its recruitment strategy for a changing higher education marketplace.

The Executive Director will preserve and strengthen Alfred State's longstanding relationships with high school counselors and other educational partners while expanding the College's reach in priority markets. Particular attention will be given to sustaining strong traditional undergraduate recruitment in New York State while increasing enrollment among out-of-state students, transfer students, online learners, and adult and professional learners.

new_jobs.description:
**The Organization**

The Mental Health Client Action Network (MHCAN) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to supporting adults in Santa Cruz County with lived experience of mental health challenges. Founded nearly 40 years ago as an independent peer support center, MHCAN is actively transitioning its operational framework to an accredited Clubhouse Model of Services.

In alignment with Clubhouse standards, MHCAN operates as a member-driven community where participants ("members") and staff work side-by-side to run daily center operations, build social connections, and pursue employment, education, and wellness goals. All MHCAN staff members share lived experience with a mental health condition and/or navigating the mental health system.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of MHCAN and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, program management, community engagement, and resource development. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director ensures the organization stays true to its core mission of peer empowerment while successfully guiding the agency through its transition to the Clubhouse model and maintaining strong alignment with County Behavioral Health.

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE / 40 hours per week) exempt position.

**Compensation:** $95,000 – $105,000 annually, depending on experience.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Human Resources & Staff Leadership (25%)**

* Hire, train, supervise, and mentor all program staff and peer support team members.
* Foster a positive, supportive, and accountable organizational culture centered on lived experience and recovery.
* Manage staff scheduling, performance evaluations, and team development.
* Partner with the Fiscal Agent (FSAS) on HR policy enforcement, workplace safety, and personnel administration.

**Program Oversight & Clubhouse Model Transition (25%)**

* Lead the agency’s transition to and ongoing operation of a certified Clubhouse model of services.
* Ensure daily program activities effectively meet client needs and contract objectives.
* Evaluate program outcomes and implement continuous service delivery improvements.
* Monitor compliance with grant deliverables and County service agreements.

**Organizational Leadership & Strategy (20%)**

* Implement the organization's mission, vision, and strategic goals, serving as a passionate advocate for peer support.
* Develop annual organizational objectives in close collaboration with the Board of Directors and the County contract monitor.
* Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable legal and nonprofit regulatory standards.
* Provide monthly performance, operational, and financial reports to the Board.

**Community Relations & County Partnership (15%)**

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for MHCAN.
* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

**Financial Oversight & Fiscal Agent Coordination (5%)**

* Develop and manage the annual operating budget (approximately $590,000) in partnership with the Board and Fiscal Agent.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director- Aurora Day Camp
new_jobs.description:
A rare opportunity to define Aurora's next chapter, deepen its impact, and build the community support and resources to sustain it.

Aurora Day Camp creates joy, connection, and community for children with cancer and their siblings.

Aurora Day Camp seeks an accomplished, entrepreneurial Executive Director to lead the organization into its next decade. Working with Sunrise Association, the local Advisory Board, staff, families, and community partners, the Executive Director will strengthen Aurora's financial foundation, raise its visibility, deepen its year-round support for families, and build stronger relationships throughout Atlanta's pediatric cancer community.

Fundraising and financial sustainability will be central to the role. The Executive Director must be a credible and effective fundraiser who can build relationships, broaden community support, and secure the resources required to carry out Aurora's priorities. This leader must also connect fundraising to a broader vision for mission impact, family engagement, strong partnerships, and organizational excellence.

**About Aurora Day Camp**

Aurora Day Camp brings back the simple joys of childhood for children with cancer and their siblings. Through a six- week summer day camp, year-round programs, and Aurora on Wheels in-hospital activities, children can play, create, build friendships, and simply be kids. Every program is offered free of charge to families.

Now entering its tenth year, Aurora has become a valued part of Atlanta's pediatric cancer community. The organization works alongside families, healthcare providers, volunteers, donors, foundations, and community partners across the region. Aurora is locally led and supported, with a seasoned Camp Director providing experienced leadership for camp and program delivery.

The Sunrise Association is both Aurora's fiscal sponsor and an important organizational partner. Sunrise provides financial administration, accreditation support, insurance, operational guidance, and access to a larger cohort of day camps serving children with cancer and their siblings across the United States and around the world. This partnership gives Aurora the benefits of established infrastructure and shared expertise while allowing it to remain deeply rooted in the Atlanta community.

**The Opportunity**

Aurora has built a strong programmatic foundation and is ready to define its next chapter. The next Executive Director will help determine where Aurora should be in three to five years and what partnerships, staffing, volunteer leadership, systems, visibility, and financial resources will be needed to deepen its impact. The opportunity is not simply to grow the number of campers. It is to make Aurora better known and supported, strengthen year-round

connections with families, deepen collaboration with Children's Healthcare of Atlanta and other pediatric cancer organizations, and establish Aurora as an essential part of Atlanta's pediatric cancer community.

This is an entrepreneurial role in a lean, approximately $1 million organization. The successful candidate will be both strategic and hands-on, equally comfortable facilitating a planning conversation, developing board leadership,

meeting with a major donor, reviewing a budget, representing Aurora in the community, and helping the team solve an immediate problem.

The Executive Director will report to Sunrise Association and work closely with Aurora's local Advisory Board. The Executive Director will directly supervise and work closely with the Camp Director. The role offers meaningful local leadership and autonomy along with the resources and accountability of a larger partner organization.

**What the Executive Director Will Lead**

**Fundraising and Financial Sustainability**

* Serve as Aurora's chief fundraiser and personally manage a portfolio of individual, corporate, and foundation prospects and donors.
* Develop and execute a diversified, multi-year fundraising strategy aligned with Aurora's strategic priorities.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors, sponsors, foundations, and corporate partners throughout Greater Atlanta.
* Lead grant strategy, proposal development, reporting, and relationship management.
* Provide leadership for Aurora's signature fundraising efforts, including the Dare to Dream Gala, AuroraWALKS, and other community events.
* Equip Advisory Board members, volunteers, and staff to succeed as ambassadors, relationship builders, and fundraising partners.

**Vision Strategy and Mission Impact**

* Partner with Sunrise Association, the Advisory Board, staff, families, and community stakeholders to articulate a compelling vision for Aurora's next decade.
* Develop and execute a practical three-to-five-year strategic roadmap with clear priorities, measurable objectives, and the resources required for success.
* Identify opportunities to deepen Aurora's support for families beyond camp, strengthen community awareness, and expand collaboration across Atlanta's pediatric cancer community.

**Board and Organizational Leadership**

* Strengthen the Advisory Board as a strategic leadership body by clarifying expectations, deepening engagement, and recruiting members whose skills, relationships, and perspectives advance Aurora's mission.
* Translate strategy into annual priorities, budgets, work plans, accountability, and measurable results.
* Directly supervise and support the Camp Director and coordinate effectively with the broader Aurora team.
* Strengthen organizational systems and oversee financial performance, budgeting, compliance, and administration in close partnership with Sunrise Association's finance and operational teams.

* Sustain Aurora's positive, mission-centered culture and create an environment in which staff members feel supported, valued, accountable, and connected to shared priorities.

**Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**

**Department:** Administration  
**Reports To:** Board of Directors  
**Location:** Roanoke, Virginia  
**Work Arrangement:** Onsite

**About Roanoke**  
Located in the heart of Virginia’s Blue Ridge region, Roanoke offers a combination of natural beauty, outdoor recreation, cultural amenities, and an accessible quality of life. As a regional center for healthcare, business, and education, the area provides the amenities of a larger community while maintaining a welcoming and connected atmosphere.

**Position Summary**

The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and operation of New Horizons Healthcare, a Federally Qualified Health Center. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO provides strategic direction and ensures the organization fulfills its mission while maintaining strong operational, financial, clinical, and regulatory performance.

The CEO works collaboratively with the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership team to establish organizational priorities, implement strategic initiatives, oversee resources, and ensure the delivery of high-quality, accessible healthcare services to the communities served.

**Compensation:** $200,000 - $250,000 annually, with compensation determined based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated leadership capabilities. New Horizons Healthcare also offers a comprehensive benefits package.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization in alignment with its mission and Board-approved goals.
* Partner with the Board of Directors and Senior Leadership team to establish priorities, implement strategies, and evaluate organizational performance.
* Oversee financial, clinical, operational, administrative, and workforce functions to ensure organizational effectiveness and sustainability.
* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, HRSA, FQHC, quality, and governance requirements.
* Develop and support organizational leadership while promoting accountability, collaboration, employee engagement, and continuous improvement.
* Maintain strong relationships with community partners, government agencies, funders, and other stakeholders.
* Represent and advocate for the organization and the healthcare needs of the communities it serves.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, or a related field required; master’s degree preferred.
* Minimum of seven (7) years of senior-level leadership experience in a nonprofit healthcare or human services organization.
* Demonstrated experience leading organizational operations, personnel, healthcare programs, and budgets.
* Community Health Center or Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) experience highly desirable.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong executive leadership, strategic planning, financial management, and decision-making skills.
* Experience developing and leading high-performing teams and managing organizational change.
* Ability to establish priorities, address complex healthcare and organizational issues, and achieve results.
* Strong communication and relationship-building skills with the Board, employees, community partners, government agencies, and other stakeholders.
* Knowledge of healthcare regulations, compliance, advocacy, and community-based healthcare.
* Capacity to manage challenging situations with fairness, sound judgment, and a focus on shared organizational goals.

**Work Environment**

This position is onsite and requires regular interaction with employees, the Board of Directors, patients, community partners, government representatives, and other external stakeholders.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

New Horizons Healthcare is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

**Organization Overview**

**Founded in 1951 by Corning Incorporated as a gift to the nation, the Corning Museum of Glass (CMoG) is the global center for the art, science, and history of glass.** The Museum shapes the understanding and appreciation of glass worldwide and draws more than 300,000 visitors each year to a city of roughly 10,000 residents. The *New York Times* named CMoG as one of the U.S. museums to see in 2025, and *Newsweek* readers voted CMoG one of the Top 3 Best Art Museums in America.

With more than 10,000 works on display, the Museum galleries showcase glass selected from a permanent collection of more than 50,000 objects representing more than 3,500 years of history. The expansive collection is presented in three core galleries – 35 Centuries of Glass, Heineman, and Contemporary Art & Design – to tell the global story of glass from antiquity through the present day. The Innovation Galleries highlight scientific and technological achievements using glass, ranging from casserole dishes to telescopes to optical fiber.

**CMoG is regarded as the conservation authority on glass to museums and institutions around the world.**

In late 2024, the Museum celebrated the expansion of The Studio, funded primarily by a successful capital campaign. The Studio, which is celebrating its 30th anniversary in 2026, features the first large scale kiln casting facility in North America and can support over 100,000 Make Your Own Glass projects annually. The state-of-the-art facilities provide artists and students with the tools and the support they need to take risks and make discoveries; opportunities for people of all skill levels to forge and deepen their understanding of glass; and connections to the glass community, where artists gather to create, learn, and share.

**Role Summary & Context for Recruitment**

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is responsible for the strategic planning, management, and success of the comprehensive fundraising efforts of the Corning Museum of Glass, including the pursuit of long-term relationships that benefit the financial health of the Museum. The CDO oversees policy, strategy, and execution of the work of the Development Department, which includes individual and planned giving, corporate, foundation and government giving, membership, giving appeals, special events, and donor relations programs. This leader reports to the Museum President and Executive Director, providing them with expert advice on all aspects of fundraising, including policy development and changes as well as new program directions. The CDO will manage all future campaigns. The CDO works closely with the Development Committee and Board of Trustees to build the Museum’s visibility, impact, and financial resources. The CDO serves as a champion for CMoG and the catalyst in strengthening the Museum’s culture of philanthropy.

The CDO oversees a team of seven staff members and provides strategic oversight and leadership for the Development Department’s annual operating budget.

Formal fundraising at CMoG is a relatively young discipline, having taken shape over the past decade alongside the Museum's landmark expansion of The Studio, and its successful capital campaign. As CMoG enters its next chapter, the Museum is investing in building a comprehensive, professionalized development program capable of matching the global stature of its collection, scholarship, and artistic community. The CDO will have the rare opportunity to help shape this program's strategy, systems, and team at an early and formative stage of its growth.

The CDO will be a close strategic partner and an active member of the Museum's leadership team. This is an opportunity to help shape CMoG's comprehensive strategic and fundraising plan, to be developed in partnership with the President and Board of Trustees over the coming year.

With a world-renowned glass collection, the preeminent Rakow Research Library, and a thriving community of working studio artists, CMoG offers an unusually rich philanthropic story. The CDO will have the opportunity to build Development’s presence among collector, scholarly, and design communities nationally and internationally, while deepening engagement with members and visitors closer to home.

* Minimum of 10 years of successful nonprofit fundraising with a track record of increased managerial responsibility and fundraising success.
* Demonstrated track record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and securing significant major gifts, coupled with experience leading and developing successful fundraising teams.
* Demonstrated experience securing corporate philanthropic support and foundation and government grants.

The Strategic Initiatives Consultant works as an embedded member of the Foundation team and participates in and supports fundraising lifecycle functions: Prospect Identification, Fundraising Strategy & Planning, Donor Engagement & Cultivation, Proposal & Solicitation Development, and Gift Negotiation & Closing.

* Strategic Campaign Counsel: Partner with the CDO to refine the external case for support, bringing commercial rigor and swift pacing to donor engagement strategies for the Renton campus.

**About Us**

**Hope. Care. Cure. These three simple words capture what we do at Seattle Children’s – to help every child live the healthiest and most fulfilling life possible. U.S. News & World Report consistently ranks Seattle Children’s among the nation’s best children’s hospitals. * Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus access to healthcare advocacy support.

The Executive Director will represent the Kansas higher education system with legislators, executive branch officials, state agencies, institutional leaders, statewide partners, and national organizations. The position requires sound political judgment, discretion, credibility, and the ability to build alignment among partners with varied interests.

* Develop and execute KBOR's legislative and governmental affairs strategy in coordination with the President and CEO.

* Monitor legislation, budgets, and policy developments affecting Kansas higher education and provide timely analysis and recommendations.
* Facilitate information sharing, coordinated planning, and consistent messaging with system partners around Board-approved legislative, budget, and policy priorities.
* Prepare briefings, testimony, talking points, reports, and other materials for senior leadership and the Board.
* Represent KBOR in legislative, governmental, public policy, and higher education forums.

**Preferred Candidate Profile**

The successful candidate will bring significant experience in government relations, legislative affairs, public policy, or a closely related field; strong knowledge of Kansas legislative and budget processes; exceptional communication and relationship-building skills; and demonstrated ability to exercise political judgment and influence without direct authority. * Experience advising senior executive leadership on legislative, policy, budgetary, governmental, or stakeholder strategy.

* Exceptional oral, written, analytical, and interpersonal communication skills.

**Position Overview**

The Assistant Director of Development and Affinity Engagement advances The Ohio State University’s philanthropic priorities by managing leadership annual giving relationships and using alumni and affinity engagement as a strategic pathway for donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and pipeline development. This hybrid position is primarily focused on cultivating and soliciting leadership annual gifts of $3,000 to $99,999, while also strengthening alumni and constituent relationships through engagement strategies that support fundraising outcomes and Advancement priorities. As a member of the Connections team within the Ohio State University Alumni Association (OSUAA), the Assistant Director proactively manages an assigned portfolio of leadership annual giving donors and prospects through in-person visits, virtual outreach, engagement opportunities, and targeted cultivation activity. The role emphasizes discovery, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of donors, identification and referral of future major gift prospects, and collaboration with volunteers and alumni leaders to advance fundraising and engagement strategies. The primary audiences for the Assistant Director include OSUAA affinity groups and Buckeye Connected Communities, with engagement activity intentionally focused on strengthening donor relationships, identifying prospective philanthropic support, and advancing leadership annual giving outcomes.

  
  

In addition to direct fundraising responsibilities, the Assistant Director serves as a liaison to select affinity groups and Buckeye Connected Communities to support engagement strategies that deepen constituent relationships and create opportunities for donor cultivation, stewardship, and pipeline development. The position also contributes to the development, execution, and evaluation of engagement programs and communications within assigned audiences or regions, ensuring those activities support Advancement priorities, donor engagement, and leadership annual giving objectives. This role requires frequent travel, including approximately two overnight trips per month, evening and weekend work, and the ability to monitor and administer an allocated budget in alignment with Advancement policies and fiscal guidelines. Success is measured through established fundraising and engagement metrics, including donor meetings, qualifications, solicitations, dollars raised, major gift referrals, first-time event attendees, and increased volunteer participation.

**Location:** Alfred, NY **Category:** Management - MC **Job Type:** Full-time In-Person **Posted On:** Fri Oct 2 2026 **Job Description:**  
  

Alfred State College seeks a dynamic, relationship-centered, and forward-thinking Executive Director of Admissions to provide strategic leadership for undergraduate admissions and recruitment.

Reporting to the Vice President for Enrollment Management, the Executive Director will lead a talented admissions team responsible for attracting, recruiting, admitting, and enrolling students who will thrive at Alfred State. The successful candidate will build upon recent enrollment momentum while helping the College evolve its recruitment strategy for a changing higher education marketplace.

The Executive Director will preserve and strengthen Alfred State's longstanding relationships with high school counselors and other educational partners while expanding the College's reach in priority markets. Particular attention will be given to sustaining strong traditional undergraduate recruitment in New York State while increasing enrollment among out-of-state students, transfer students, online learners, and adult and professional learners.

* **A College Preparing for Its Next Strategic Chapter** - Alfred State is completing a successful five-year strategic plan in which its established goals have been achieved. Monitor My Health, Inc., a Connecticut-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, is seeking a highly organized and motivated **Program & Grants Assistant to the Chief Operating Officer (COO)**.

This position is ideal for someone with experience in **grant writing or grant assistance, nonprofit programs, program development, and/or reporting** who wants hands-on experience supporting the planning and implementation of community health programs.

***Key Responsibilities***

The Program & Grants Assistant will work directly with the COO and assist with:

* Grant writing, including researching opportunities, drafting grant applications, gathering supporting information, and preparing required documents
* Grant and program reports, including collecting and organizing program data and assisting with narrative reports
* Program planning, development, and implementation
* Developing work plans, timelines, program materials, and supporting documents
* Research related to new programs, funding opportunities, and community needs
* Tracking grant requirements, deadlines, deliverables, and program milestones
* Preparing documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and other materials
* Assisting with partner and stakeholder communications
* Supporting the COO with other program development and administrative projects as needed

***Qualifications***

**Required:**

* Previous experience with **grant writing or assisting with grant applications**
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail
* Ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines
* Strong research and professional writing skills
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and/or Google Workspace
* Ability to work independently while taking direction and feedback

**Preferred:**

* Experience working with a nonprofit, healthcare, public health, human services, or community-based organization
* Experience with program planning, program implementation, grant reporting, or program evaluation
* Experience preparing reports or working with program data

***Schedule & Work Arrangement***

This position is approximately **15 hours per week** and will initially be **in person**.

Our preferred workdays are **Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday**. The selected candidate may work **two to three of these days**, depending on the agreed-upon schedule and organizational needs.

* **$25.00 per hour**
* Approximately **15 hours per week**
* **1099 independent contractor position**

We are looking for someone who is dependable, detail-oriented, comfortable with writing, and genuinely interested in helping develop and expand nonprofit community health programs.

Pay: $25.00 per hour
